items.title: Ozone hole one of the largest in decades
items.summary: In contrast to the 2025 seasonal ozone hole above Antarctica, which was the fifth smallest since 1992, this year's ozone hole ranks as one of the largest in 48 years, based on long-term atmospheric observations, including data from the Copernicus Sentinel-5P satellite. While this may sound alarming, it is important to remember that the size of the ozone hole varies naturally from year to year, and the long-term recovery of the ozone layer remains on track.

items.title: As families gather for Thanksgiving, college science students need training to talk across societal divides
items.summary: Most Americans have seen it happen. Relatives argue online about whether vaccines are safe and effective. Friends and neighbors trade jabs over climate change and whether anything should be done about it. Public officials and scientists disagree, loudly, about what causes autism or which vaccines children should get and when. No one gives an inch, and the rifts rarely heal. This Thanksgiving, after a contentious election season, many of those conversations will happen face to face around the dinner table.
